glaux: Why do some stars glow blue, while others glow like embers?
Before I explain, take a guess: which one is hottest? No points. I'm just nosy.

cards.glaux: Colour is a clue, even across the dark.
cards.text: Stars come in many colours. Blue stars have the hottest surfaces. Red stars are cooler, though still fiercely hot.

cards.glaux: Heavier stars have a lot to say.
cards.text: Mass means how much stuff a star holds. In their long, steady stage, heavier stars are bigger and hotter.

cards.glaux: More fuel does not always mean more time. Let's look closer.
cards.text: They use up their fuel, a light gas called hydrogen, faster. So they live shorter lives.

cards.glaux: This part gets me every time.
cards.text: A very heavy star may shine for only a few million years. The Sun shines for about ten billion. Slide along the line and feel the gap.

cards.glaux: Keep these three small clues. We will meet them again.
items: Blue stars are hotter than red stars.
Heavier stars are usually bigger and hotter.
Heavier stars use fuel faster and live shorter lives.
